quotes.text: If your video fails, it's okay. The meeting can still go on. You can still hear people with audio. If your audio fails, now you're done. Your meeting is over.
quotes.speaker: Josh Blalock
quotes.why: A memorable, simple argument for prioritising audio over video in meeting rooms.

quotes.text: It's no longer just spoken words and audio. Now audio is actually real-time data that co-pilot is going to use to do a whole bunch of stuff to build documents, to create task lists, to send emails
quotes.speaker: Josh Blalock
quotes.why: Reframes meeting-room audio as the data source for Copilot.

quotes.text: businesses have to stop thinking about their spend in the meeting room as good enough. They now have to think about the fact that they are building the foundational layer for all the AI investment that they are making in the platform.
quotes.speaker: Josh Blalock
quotes.why: Connects meeting-room hardware budgets directly to AI ROI.

quotes.text: ensuring that the audio is as clean as it can be before it ever gets to Microsoft is really the key to having the best data for your AI on the back end.
quotes.speaker: Josh Blalock
quotes.why: Explains why on-device audio processing matters even with cloud cleanup.

quotes.text: support is the other angle where certification matters. You want to get support from Microsoft? Make sure you're using a certified solution in that space.
quotes.speaker: Josh Blalock
quotes.why: Practical buying advice: certification determines Microsoft support.

takeaways: In AI-enabled meetings, audio is no longer just sound but the real-time data Copilot uses for summaries, action items and documents, so 'good enough' audio limits your AI investment.
Clean audio should be produced in the room, for example by onboard software DSPs in microphones and room kits, before Microsoft Teams processes it in the cloud.
Teams certified devices pass rigorous Microsoft testing and are the supported option, and complex rooms still benefit from an integrator, a proof of concept and acoustic treatment.
hook: Most organizations still treat meeting-room audio as an afterthought, even though Copilot now depends on it. In this episode, Microsoft MVP Josh Blalock explains to IT leaders and meeting-room planners how Teams evolved from Skype for Business, why audio beats video, what Teams certification really means and how to plan rooms that give AI clean data.
